lines: This is KOMA.
An AI comic studio, and a series launchpad, on Arbitrum.
You describe a story. KOMA writes it, draws it and letters it in about a minute.
Ten cents a page in USDC, minted to your wallet on Arbitrum.
Let's make one. I give the editor an idea: a delivery girl racing a thunderstorm across Neo Tokyo.
It pitches a title, a story, a style, a cast, and a price.
Paying is one signature. An x402 USDC authorization. No gas, no account.
KOMA's facilitator settles it on Arbitrum. Then the script is written, the panels are drawn and lettered, live.
And the issue is minted straight to my wallet.
Every issue is an ERC-721 that stores a hash of its pages and the payment that bought it.
The payment decodes on-chain, and the receipts ledger shows every settled payment.
Reading is free. Every panel and every balloon comes straight from the model.
And because it's plain x402, any AI agent can buy a comic too. One HTTP call, a 402, a signature. Done.
Now, the launchpad. Every series is a character, with its own coin.
The board shows what's trending, what's about to graduate, and a live tape of every launch, trade and canon decision, straight from the chain.
Launching a series costs one dollar. I name it, pick a ticker, and describe the hero.
One signature, and KOMA draws a character sheet, then launches everything in a single transaction.
A Character NFT with its own ERC-6551 wallet, and a coin on a USDC bonding curve.
That sheet keeps the character on model in every episode.
Trading is gasless. A five dollar buy is one USDC signature, and KOMA's relayer pays the gas.
The signature locks the amount, the minimum out and the deadline, so the relayer can't change them.
Selling is a permit plus a signed intent.
Every trade pays one and a half percent. Forty to the character's wallet, twenty up the remix tree, forty to KOMA.
And forty percent lands in the character's own ERC-6551 wallet, which whoever holds the Character NFT can withdraw.
Holders write the canon. As the character's owner, I propose the next episode, right in the studio.
It's drawn with the character sheet, so Juniper stays on model, and it's minted and entered as a proposal.
Holders vote for free, with an EIP-712 signature, weighted by what they held when voting opened.
When the clock runs out, KOMA's keeper writes the winner, and a Merkle root of every vote, to the canon registry on-chain.
When a curve hits its target, it graduates. The Last Bowl already has.
KOMA takes five percent, and the keeper moves the rest into a Uniswap v4 pool, locked for good, with KOMA's Graduator as its hook.
Trading carries on in the pool. Still one signature, still gasless.
Remixes are new series in the same world. Moon Bowl remixes The Last Bowl, and part of every Moon Bowl fee flows back to its parent.
Under the hood, it's all Arbitrum.
The curve math and the royalty router are Rust contracts on Arbitrum Stylus, live and verified on Arbitrum Sepolia.
Plus gasless intents, x402 payments, ERC-6551 wallets and Uniswap v4.
KOMA. Write it. We draw it.
Your characters. Your canon. On Arbitrum.
